issue_context.title: Nullish event handler produces TypeError
issue_context.body:
### Describe the bug

Some event handlers, such as `onmouseenter` or `onmouseleave`, throw an error when set to `null`/`undefined` instead of not registering the event handler.

### Reproduction

https://svelte.dev/playground/fa643cc4e0ed4434bb6ba9bc5a5a8ec0?version=5.19.1

### Logs

```shell
TypeError
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'call')
    at eval (playground:output:2036:21)
    at without_reactive_context (playground:output:2004:11)
    at HTMLButtonElement.target_handler (playground:output:2035:12)
```

### System Info

```shell
Svelte 5.19.1 (Playground)
```

### Severity

blocking an upgrade
comments: The reason for that is if you look at the compiled output, you'll notice that for `onclick`, it assigns a property of the button to the event handler, while with the other event, it calls a function. In the function, it runs `Element.addEventListener`, which throws if the provided handler is not a function. You shouldn't have a nullish event handler (partly because there's no reason to).

> partly because there's no reason to

Well, just because you can't think of a use case doesn't mean there's no reason.

> You shouldn't have a nullish event handler

This worked fine in Svelte 4 (see [this](https://github.com/sveltejs/svelte/issues/7568) feature request). And I didn't find in the documentation that there should be any changes in this regard in Svelte 5. On the contrary, the documentation clearly says that _**events are just attributes, the same rules as for attributes apply**_. And for attributes it says that _**attributes are included unless their value is nullish (null or undefined)**_.

Based on this, I believe that either this is a regression in Svelte 5 and needs to be fixed, or the fact that some events are now registered even with nullish handler needs to be documented.

I agree that this needs to be fixed both for consistency and because it might be good to remove a listener once not needed.

Gonna fix this later.
@paoloricciuti Thank you for the quick fix of the bug.

review_comments: we should probably also adjust the call signature to allow undefined for the handler param, and adjust that for `export function event(...)` aswell
Oh good catch...gonna fix them soon
